summary: BYU’s first loss came 39-31 in double overtime at UCF. Tackling and drive continuity lead the response before Arizona State; the November 7 rivalry game now has a 10 a.m. MT kickoff.

items.headline: BYU loses 39-31 at UCF in double overtime
items.tldr: The Cougars return home to face Arizona State at 1:30 p.m. MT Saturday on FOX. Watch the response in ordinary possessions before another finish becomes the whole game.

items.headline: Missed tackles put the defense under pressure
items.tldr: Deseret News examines UCF’s production after the catch and on the ground. Johnson’s late injury was still being evaluated in the report; avoid assuming a return date.

items.headline: Four three-and-outs limit BYU’s scoring chances
items.tldr: Deseret News counts four empty three-play possessions in the loss. The offense needs a dependable first-down answer alongside its longer completions.

items.headline: Moa returns for his first game since the opener
items.tldr: KSL reports 13 carries for 36 yards and a touchdown. Watch how the backfield’s available personnel can support the rushing attack without assuming Martin is cleared.

items.headline: BYU–Utah will kick at 10 a.m. MT on November 7
items.tldr: The rivalry game will air on ABC or ESPN, with the network still to be selected. Arizona State comes first; the new window helps fans plan the following weekend.

lead.headline: Finish the tackle, sustain the drive.
lead.body: Close the space after the catch with a balanced first tackle and connected pursuit. On offense, make the first carry and quick throw useful enough to keep the next possession alive.

matchup.thesis: Give both units a repeatable answer
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Use protection and route spacing to earn another set of downs. Defend the catch with leverage and a second tackler so a short completion does not become the opponent’s easiest long gain.
